_comment: Cell-runtime fence register — INPUT to tests/test_dependency_license_fence.py, not prose.
What this guards, stated without a licence story: Ephe binds a cell runtime that we build,
measure and audit ourselves. `core/cpython_cell.py` writes a WASIConfig from its own `DEFAULT_*`
caps and `core/cell_policy.policy_snapshot()` reports exactly those values (max_fuel,
max_memory_mb, timeout_seconds, network=none) to the settings card, `ephe doctor` and the status
page, under one rule: report == enforced. That identity only holds for the release we measured.
A pin that moves to an unmeasured release is not a licence problem — Ephemora Cell is our own
product, so BUSL-1.1 binds nobody here — it is the settings surface quoting caps from a runtime
whose enforcement we have not re-read. So the fence asks ONE question of every release a bound
admits: has this codebase measured its policy against it, and is that measurement still inside
its re-check window.
Licences are still recorded per release, for two reasons: they are a fact about the artifact, and
`tests/test_dependency_license_fence.py` cross-checks the recorded value against the installed
dist-info, so a register that drifts from what is actually installed fails. Recording is not
fencing — nothing here blocks a version on its licence, and no version was ever chosen for one.
Per-release evidence, the way the repo does evidence elsewhere (`proven`):
"artifact"  — METADATA and the `licenses/LICENSE` file unpacked from that exact wheel, sha256
checked against PyPI's digest.
"index"     — a registry field only; never usable as fence evidence.
A version with no entry stops the run: read that wheel, measure the policy, add a line.
`policy_measured: null` is therefore an explicit statement — we have NOT measured it.

ephemora-cell.reason: The pin holds the one release whose cell policy this codebase measured; moving it is a re-measurement task, not an upgrade.
ephemora-cell.policy_source: core/cpython_cell.py DEFAULT_MAX_FUEL / DEFAULT_MAX_MEMORY_MB / DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and core/cell_policy.policy_snapshot()

1.0.4.3.license_note: METADATA declares Apache-2.0 plus the OSI Apache classifier; the wheel's licenses/LICENSE is the Apache text. Its sha256 equals the hash uv.lock already carries, so this register and the lock point at the same bytes.
1.0.4.3.policy_evidence: Enforcement read from the installed runtime: ephemora_cell/__init__.py:103 run_isolated always dispatches to process_executor.run_isolated (a disposable worker subprocess), which is the path where disk_quota_bytes is enforced through RLIMIT_FSIZE and a guest panic costs the worker, not Ephe.

1.0.5.license_note: METADATA `License: BUSL-1.1`, no OSI classifier, licenses/LICENSE is the BUSL text (Licensor: the dependency's own licensor, Additional Use Grant: None, Change License Apache-2.0 at the fourth anniversary). Our own product, so it constrains nothing; recorded because the register states what is installed.
1.0.5.policy_evidence: Not measured. API read from the wheel: WASIConfig carries the same 13 fields as 1.0.4.3, so the call in core/cpython_cell.py:189 stays valid — but the fuel-per-second and I/O enforcement figures in core/cpython_cell.py:22-23 were measured on 1.0.4.3 and were not re-run.

1.1.0.license_note: Same BUSL text as 1.0.5; newest release on PyPI as of 2026-10-09.
1.1.0.policy_evidence: Not measured. API read from the wheel: WASIConfig *adds* allow_fsync and max_wasm_bytes and removes nothing, so the additive change is compatible with our call site; the engine requirement is `wasmtime<48,>=43.0.1` in 1.0.4.3, 1.0.5 and 1.1.0 alike, which is why no release of this package reaches the wasmtime-wasi fix at 48.0.3 (see .github/engine-advisories.txt).
